newsitem.title: USA: Firefighters make progress on California wildfire.
newsitem.headline: Firefighters make progress on California wildfire.

text.p: Firefighters said they made progress on Saturday in taming a wildfire that forced the evacuation of dozens of homes and businesses and the closure of a highway along a scenic stretch of California coast.
The fire broke out Friday afternoon in a canyon near the town of Big Sur, about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.

The fire, burning in the Ventana wilderness area of the Los Padres National Forest, an area famous for its natural beauty, grew to 650 acres (260 hectares) on Saturday, said fire information officer David Schreiner.

Firefighters had the fire 45 percent contained by Saturday evening, but there was no estimate of when the blaze, burning in rugged forest and brushland, would be fully contained, Schreiner said. "We're making progress," he said.
Firefighters ordered the evacuation of houses and businesses along a five-mile (eight-km) stretch on the east side of Highway One, a popular route that winds along the California coast.

About 25 homes and a half-dozen businesses, including the well-known Ventana Inn, which lies about two miles (three kms) south of Big Sur, remained evacuated on Saturday evening. An evacuation centre was set up at a Big Sur school for residents to spend the night, Schreiner said. A 37-mile (60-km) section of Highway One was closed.
One travel trailer had been destroyed but so far no homes had been lost and there had been no injuries, Schreiner said.
About 980 firefighters were battling the blaze, backed by nine air tankers and eight helicopters, Schreiner said.
The cause of the fire was unknown and was under investigation.

Ironically, the new fire broke out just about two hours before a 25,000-acre (10,000-hectare) blaze that had burned for 12 days about 30 miles (50 kms) away in the Los Padres National Forest was declared fully under control.
Because many firefighters were in the area, fire officials were able to divert lots of resources to the new fire.
